## Introduction

For this post, I wanted to see how some basic physical measurements differ
between the three penguin species in the Palmer Penguins dataset. I focused on
body mass and flipper length because both give a simple way to compare the
species.

Data source: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. Data are available under a CC0 license.

## Exploring the data

I started by loading the data and looking at the first few rows.

```{python}
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()

penguins.head()
```

Next, I checked the size of the dataset and the columns available.

```{python}
print("Rows and columns:", penguins.shape)
penguins.columns
```

There are several measurements available, but for this post I am mainly
interested in `species`, `body_mass_g`, and `flipper_length_mm`.

## Comparing the species

I grouped the penguins by species and calculated the average body mass and
flipper length for each group.

```{python}
species_summary = penguins.groupby("species")[
    ["body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm"]
].mean()

species_summary = species_summary.round(1)

species_summary
```

This gives me one row for each species instead of one row for each individual
penguin. The differences are already pretty noticeable, especially for Gentoo
penguins.

## Visualizing body mass

I used the species averages to compare body mass visually.

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass
#| fig-cap: "Average body mass of Palmer penguins by species."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

species_summary["body_mass_g"].plot(
    kind="bar",
    figsize=(7, 4)
)

plt.title("Gentoo penguins are heavier on average")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Average body mass (g)")
plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Gentoo penguins stand out immediately. Their average body mass is much higher
than the other two species, while Adelie penguins have the lowest average.

## Looking at flipper length

Since Gentoo penguins were also larger in the summary table, I wanted to look
at flipper length separately.

```{python}
species_summary["flipper_length_mm"].sort_values()
```

The same general pattern appears here. Gentoo penguins have the longest
flippers on average, while Adelie penguins have the shortest.

## What I noticed

The species differ quite a bit in both measurements. Gentoo penguins are the
heaviest of the three on average and also have the longest flippers. Adelie
penguins are smaller on both measurements, with Chinstrap penguins falling
between them.

This is a small analysis, but it was a useful way to see how grouping the data
can make differences between categories much easier to spot.
